interactions.summary: The student reads Virgil's account of love as the soul's motion toward beauty and of free will as the inborn power that can curb or redirect desire.

Jiang calls this the decisive speech between Dante and Virgil and translates it into a dating scenario: Virgil's model of love aims to possess the beautiful other, whereas Dante's love begins by learning the person.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang interpretive monologue with a brief class prompt.

claims.claim: The reading defines love as the soul's propensity to turn toward beauty and rest only when the beloved thing makes it joyous.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted Dante/Virgil discourse read in lecture on 2026-06-26.

claims.claim: The same passage says ethics becomes possible because, even if loves arise necessarily, an inborn keeper at the threshold can curb and sort them, which Beatrice later names free will.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted Dante/Virgil discourse read in lecture on 2026-06-26.

claims.claim: Jiang treats this free-will discussion as the defining debate that prepares for Dante and Virgil's eventual separation.
Jiang's modern analogy presents Virgil's conception of love as the soul expanding outward to possess, dominate, or control another beautiful soul.
In contrast, Jiang implies that Dante's love starts by praise, attention, and getting to know the other person rather than immediately trying to own them.

signature_moments.moment: Even if desire flares by necessity, the power to curb it remains your own.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the power to curb that love is still your own
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It captures the free-will thesis Jiang needs for both moral responsibility and later political critique.

signature_moments.moment: Virgil's love is possession: the soul wants to encompass and dominate beauty.
signature_moments.source_phrase: your soul wants to encompass ... literally dominate, control, another person
signature_moments.why_it_matters: Jiang translates a dense scholastic account of love into a vivid relational critique that will drive the rest of the discussion.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The inborn evaluative power that judges and reins in other desires, grounding moral responsibility.

chronology_notes.note: This June 26 packet is a hinge: the formal free-will doctrine is immediately re-expressed by Jiang as a conflict between possessive Virgilian love and attentive Dantean love.
